# polyline-benchmark

> Correctness checks and benchmarks for every JavaScript library that encodes and decodes Google encoded polylines, on Bun, Node 22 to 26, Deno and Chrome. It's a repository to run, not a package to install. It includes polytini (`@duoquote/polytini`), which the same author wrote, so read its rows knowing that.

What it measures: calls per second for `encode()` and `decode()` on lines of 10 to 100,000 points and on 1000 real-world lines (median 82 points), plus typed arrays, batch calls, memory per call and gzipped bundle size. Every library has to pass the same correctness test before it's timed.

How to read the numbers: a cell moves about 30% between rounds, so a gap under about 30% between the top libraries isn't a reliable ranking. The "best at what" table marks those. Libraries are only compared within one runtime. CI runs the correctness tests only, never the benchmark.

Run it:

```sh
npm ci
npm test              # correctness, every library
npm run bench:quick   # about a minute, writes nothing
npm run bench:all     # everything, about 10 minutes, writes results/
```

## Docs

- [README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Duoquote/polyline-benchmark/main/README.md): the best-at-what table and the Bun and Node 24 results
- [Results](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Duoquote/polyline-benchmark/main/docs/results.md): every runtime, relative speed, typed arrays, batch calls, memory and sizes
- [Methodology](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Duoquote/polyline-benchmark/main/docs/methodology.md): the library list, the correctness cases, how timing and memory are measured, and the run options
- [AGENTS.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Duoquote/polyline-benchmark/main/AGENTS.md): how to work in the repo and add a library

## Optional

- [Charts](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Duoquote/polyline-benchmark/main/docs/charts.md): every chart, generated from results/
- [polytini](https://github.com/Duoquote/polytini): the codec this benchmark led to, with its own llms.txt
